autoSelect.title: ⚙️ Automatic selection
autoSelect.description: Rules are applied from top to bottom — for each game, the last matching rule wins. BIOS, devices and removed games are not affected (they are handled automatically by the dependency cascade).
autoSelect.presetNoProtoTitle: Adds rules excluding entries whose name or description contains (Proto, (Beta, (Demo, (Sample, Prototype
autoSelect.presetNoBiosTitle: Adds a rule excluding [BIOS] entries (No-Intro/Redump convention — MAME BIOSes are already handled by the dependency cascade)
autoSelect.presetNoAftermarketTitle: Adds rules excluding entries whose name or description contains (Aftermarket) and (Unl) (No-Intro/Redump convention)
autoSelect.presetNoClonesTitle: Adds a rule excluding clones (games with a parent)
autoSelect.presetGoodOnlyTitle: Adds a rule excluding games whose MAME driver is not "good"
autoSelect.presetNoChdTitle: Adds a rule excluding games requiring a CHD
autoSelect.presetCompleteOnlyTitle: Adds a rule excluding games not complete in the matching
autoSelect.presetNoMechanicalTitle: Adds a rule excluding electromechanical machines (pinball, slot machines… — not playable with a gamepad, e.g. for a Recalbox set)
autoSelect.presetPlayableTitle: Keeps only playable games: excludes the "preliminary" and "not specified" emulation statuses (keeps good + imperfect)
autoSelect.saveDefaultTitle: Save the current rules as the default template for this kind of DAT
autoSelect.restoreDefaultTitle: Reload the default template saved for this kind of DAT
autoSelect.customSaveTitle: Save the current rules as a custom preset
autoSelect.customApplyTitle: Add this preset's rules to the current rules

archives.bestCompression: Try all compatible formats and keep the smallest
archives.bestCompressionWarning:
⚠️ WARNING: This option slows down the process CONSIDERABLY!

The application will create an archive in EVERY compatible format for each game and keep only the one with the smallest size.

  • Processing time: 3x to 5x slower
  • CPU usage: Maximum
  • Disk usage: Temporarily doubled

Recommended only if final disk space is critical.
archives.bestCompressionInfo: For each game, all compatible archive variants are created, then only the most compact one is kept (very slow)
archives.solidInfo: Solid compression improves the compression ratio but slows down extraction
archives.multithreadingInfo: Uses multiple processor cores to speed up compression

arcade.setModeInfo: Specific to MAME DATs (with parent / clone / BIOS relationships). Determines how RUMCET will organize your ROMs on disk after consolidation. This setting is ignored for non-arcade DATs (No-Intro / Redump). See docs/arcade-set-modes.md for details on the modes and their differences.
arcade.split: Split — each clone contains only its own ROMs
arcade.splitInfo: The parent and BIOS remain separate archives. Compact, but each clone depends on the parent + BIOS to work. Recommended mode.
arcade.nonMergedInfo: The clone's archive contains its own ROMs AND the ROMs shared with its parent. Large (duplication), but each game works without depending on the parent (the BIOS remains separate).
arcade.merged: Merged — one archive per family (parent + all its clones)
arcade.mergedInfo: The parent's archive contains the ROMs of the parent and all its clones. Very compact, but incompatible with some emulators that expect a separate archive per game.
arcade.layoutInfo: How files are laid out in the target folder after consolidation. Specific to MAME DATs.
arcade.separateBiosInfo: BIOS sets (isbios) are stored in bios/ instead of flat alongside games.
arcade.separateBiosWarning:
⚠️ Incompatible with standard MAME

Original MAME expects BIOS archives in the same folder as the ROMs. If you move them into bios/, games that depend on them will not launch, unless your frontend supports a separate BIOS path (Recalbox convention).
arcade.chdEmptyZip: Create an empty .zip for CHD-only games
arcade.chdEmptyZipInfo: For a game with no regular ROMs (CHD only), creates an empty <game>.zip placeholder next to the <game>/ subfolder. Recalbox lists games via the .zip files present. Implies storing the CHD in a subfolder.

oneGameOneRom.title: 1G1R — 1 game, 1 ROM
oneGameOneRom.enableInfo: When disabled, nothing changes: RUMCET behaves exactly as it does without this feature. When enabled, automatic selection keeps a single version per game, arbitrating variants according to the priorities below. The selection stays fully editable by hand afterwards.
oneGameOneRom.priorityInfo: The first entry of each list wins. A value missing from a list is not excluded: it simply comes last. To firmly exclude a region or a language, use an automatic selection rule.
oneGameOneRom.regionPriority: Regions, from most to least preferred:
oneGameOneRom.languagePriority: Languages, from most to least preferred:
oneGameOneRom.videoPriority: Video modes, from most to least preferred:
oneGameOneRom.languageOverRegionInfo: To prefer "the French version wherever it comes from" rather than "the Europe version".
oneGameOneRom.preferLatestRevisionInfo: At equal regional quality, (Rev 2) beats (Rev 1), which beats the original untagged edition.
oneGameOneRom.fallbackToOwned: Fall back to a version I own
oneGameOneRom.fallbackToOwnedInfo: When the preferred version is missing from your collection but another one is present, keep the one you have instead of leaving a hole. This is what a tool working from the DAT file alone cannot do: it has no idea what you actually own. Uncheck for a strict 1G1R computed on the DAT alone.
oneGameOneRom.cloneListInfo: The same game is sometimes released under unrelated names depending on the region (Pokémon Version Or / Pokémon Goldene Edition / Pocket Monsters Kin). No title analysis can guess that: these relations are editorial data, curated by hand by the community. RUMCET consumes them without maintaining them.
oneGameOneRom.cloneListSourceInfo: URL of the folder containing the .json files. Editable on purpose: this is what keeps RUMCET independent from the fate of any single repository.
oneGameOneRom.cloneListFolderInfo: Leave empty to use the application data folder.
oneGameOneRom.cloneListAutoApply: Re-apply automatically after each DAT load
oneGameOneRom.cloneListAutoApplyInfo: Loading a primary DAT wipes and rewrites the games table: the groupings set by a clone list disappear with it. Loading a complementary DAT adds games that do not have any yet. Without this option, you have to reopen “Auto select” and click “Apply” every time.
oneGameOneRom.cloneListAutoDownload: Download the missing list before applying it
oneGameOneRom.cloneListAutoDownloadInfo: Sub-option of the previous one. On DAT load, if no local clone list matches the system, it is downloaded then applied. A list already present is never re-downloaded: refreshing stays a manual action.
oneGameOneRom.cloneListAttribution: The clone list format and the default repository come from the Retool project by unexpectedpanda, under the BSD-3-Clause licence. RUMCET is neither its author nor its maintainer. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
